blocks.text: CANBERRA, Australia — The Solomon Islands will sign a sweeping treaty with Australia on Wednesday, a move its leader says will help build a safer region and that analysts say could hinder China’s prospects for establishing a military presence in the Pacific. Prime Minister Matthew Wale and 15 ministers arrived in Australia on Tuesday for talks covering security, infrastructure, education, and health, as well as the formal signing of the Australia-Solomon Islands Treaty. The treaty commits the two countries to shared security, contributing to a “safer and more prosperous Solomon Islands and region,” Wale said Tuesday. It has been a diplomatic […]...
